layout_notes: The Circuit runs CLOCKWISE ONLY. Late apex is the theme of nearly every corner -- both primary sources say it independently.

Zones here are keyed to the 10-turn scheme the coaching sources use (Turn 8 is the two-part 8A/8B complex). BRP's current official map numbers only 1-9. The guide binds to your Circuit layout profile by lap length (2.567 mi = 4,131 m) via layout-aware loading (v2.17.0) -- but the zone NUMBERS only match your driving once your detected corner map for this layout is checked against them; if detection splits 8A/8B or merges a pair, this guide gets re-keyed, the same drill as corner naming.

Garagistic nicknamed every corner (Captain America, Waltz, Off-camber, Slingshot, Bank, Concrete Jungle, Sunset, Congress, Setup, Swing). They are deliberately NOT used as zone names here -- his Turn 7 'Sunset' would collide with the classic track's Sunset corner in any report that mentions both layouts. Numbers only, until you name them yourself.

Brake markers are scarce all over this track (the PCA guide's recurring theme) -- in the sim as at the real track, build your own references in the first laps. Several corners have helpful positive camber/banking and carry more speed than they first appear to.

source.channel: CCCR PCA (Porsche Club of America, California Central Coast Region)
source.layout_note: Written turn-by-turn for a May 2025 driver-education day on the new Circuit: pit entry/exit, then T-1 through T-10 (T-8A/T-8B) with braking markers, speeds and photos. Cross-checked against the Garagistic video guide (Spec E30) -- the two agree on the line and apex points; their braking depths bracket by car.
source.title: Buttonwillow 'The Circuit' Walkthrough Guide

sources.note: Most-watched Circuit guide (13,009 views, Feb 2025); Spec E30, ~150 hp. Despite the title it is a Garagistic production, not a BRP video.

sources.title: Turn-by-Turn Breakdown of Buttonwillow's New Circuit (Track 2)

sources.note: Spec Racer Ford Gen3 race lap with per-turn notes in the description (Jan 2026); not separately distilled.
sources.title: 1:51.816 lap at Buttonwillow The Circuit

1.character: Fast right-hander at the end of the front straight -- the fastest approach on the track (130 mph in the PCA author's GT4), and the wall comes up quickly. Set up on the left; the references are three small cones on the left with a faint line across the pavement at the first one, and a corner station on the right. Brake and downshift in a straight line, hard -- then, for the very late apex, release most of the brake but keep some pressure on to keep the front weighted as you turn in. Apex right against the curbing, back to throttle, and let the car run out to the left. Watch your left on exit: pit entry merges onto the track parallel to this corner.
1.name: Turn 1

tips.text: Fastest approach on the track and the wall comes up quick -- brake and downshift in a straight line off the left-side cone markers, and work the point deeper gradually.
Very late apex: release most of the brake but keep the front weighted, apex on the curbing, then throttle and let it run out -- and remember pit-entry traffic merges on your left here.

10.character: A wide, fast left-hander -- 'the Swing' -- and a high-speed lift corner, not a braking corner. From far right, a brief lift of the throttle is all it takes to start the car rotating left; mid-to-late apex, very close to the curbs, then straight back to throttle and let it swing out to the right with your foot to the floor. One trap: at first your eyes will follow the pit-exit road on the left instead of the corner -- look for Turn 10 itself. Then drift back to the far left down the straight, because the Turn 1 braking point arrives fast.
10.name: Turn 10

tips.text: No brake here -- a brief lift rotates it, then straight back to throttle at the mid-late apex, tight to the curbs. Get your eyes on Turn 10 itself, not the pit exit beside it.

2.character: Mid-speed left-hander, another late apex, running uphill then downhill -- and it sneaks up on you, because the run from Turn 1 is short. Get all the way back to the right after Turn 1. Almost no brake markers, so start conservative. Positive camber through here and into Turn 3 gives more grip than you expect: after the initial brake you should be accelerating through the apex. The exit matters beyond the corner itself -- 2 and 3 flow together, and a good exit is Turn 3's momentum. A slightly later turn-in than feels natural straightens the 2-to-3 run and pays on the exit.
2.name: Turn 2

tips.text: This one sneaks up after Turn 1. A later turn-in straightens the run into Turn 3 -- the exit here is Turn 3's momentum, and the camber helps more than you think.
Turning in early here strangles the exit into Turn 3. Stay patient, apex late, and be accelerating through it.

3.character: Mid-speed right with a late apex, running slightly downhill. The PCA line stays TIGHT into it (some drivers go wider with a later apex): just before entry, a dab of brake -- less to slow the car than to load the front tires and rotate it. The exit falls away, and Garagistic flags possible lift-off oversteer in some cars, so from rotation onward it's maintenance throttle, adding gas gradually as the car settles, tracking out to the curbs on the left. (The two sources describe the camber differently -- helpful banking in the 2-3 complex per the PCA, an off-camber feel at this exit per Garagistic; the falling-away exit is the part both agree matters.)
3.name: Turn 3

tips.text: The exit falls away downhill -- a mid-corner lift can bring the rear around. Dab the brake before entry to load the front and rotate, then maintenance throttle, feeding gas in gradually.

4.character: A fast right-hander, a bit more than 90 degrees, slightly banked ('the Slingshot'). Stay left out of Turn 3 and look for a mid-to-late apex. How much slowing it needs is car-dependent: a light lift in a low-power car, a light brake in the GT4. The corner's whole value is its exit -- get the car turned in and planted so you can be back to throttle early and carry speed onto the long straight that follows. Enter a few feet off the edge, bring it down to the right curbing at the apex, and let it carry back out to the left.
4.name: Turn 4

tips.text: Exit speed is the whole corner -- it slingshots onto a long straight. Get it turned and planted, then back to throttle as early as you can.
Fast and slightly banked: many cars need only a light lift or a brush of brake here. Don't over-slow it.

5.character: The Bank: a heavily banked right ('Chuckwalla-style', per Garagistic) with a very late turn-in and a very late apex. Off the straight from Turn 4, bring the car back to the right and brake -- how hard depends on the car: a genuine heavy brake in the GT4, down to a lift or light brake in a light car; the right-side marker cones are hard to see at speed, so find your own reference in the first laps. The banking and positive camber carry far more speed than first laps suggest -- the PCA author says he went too slow into it all day. Enter about a car width off the left edge, apex touching the left-side curb, then accelerate and track out to about mid-track (faster cars further right), and come back left of mid to set up Turn 6. The exit runs uphill.
5.name: Turn 5

tips.text: The braking here is real, but the banking carries more speed than your first laps will believe -- the PCA author was too slow into it all day. Find your own marker early; the cones on the right vanish at speed.
Very late turn-in, very late apex: enter a car width off the left edge and don't drift to the curb early.

6.character: A big U-turn (a mid-speed hairpin) with concrete barriers on both sides -- Garagistic's 'Concrete Jungle' -- and some positive camber. It reads slower than it is. Standard late apex: enter about a car width off the right, come down to the right curb at the apex, and get back to throttle sooner than you think. Second or third gear depending on the car. The exit feeds a long downhill straight, so the throttle point pays twice.
6.name: Turn 6

tips.text: Late apex, and throttle sooner than it looks -- this exit feeds a long downhill straight, so the early pedal pays twice.
Slowest-feeling corner on the track, concrete on both sides -- but it carries more speed than it looks. Don't park it.

7.character: Medium-speed left, slightly banked, leading to a short straight. Full throttle out of Turn 6 and up to the right edge, then a solid brake -- a corner worker on your left and brake markers on your right are the references. Apex just past mid-corner, all the way to the left-side curbing; there's a bump right at the apex, and feeling it is how you know you found it. Accelerate at the apex and let the car carry out to the right-edge curbing.
7.name: Turn 7

tips.text: Solid brake, apex just past mid, all the way to the left curbing -- there's a bump at the apex; feeling it means you found it.

8.character: The slowest and possibly hardest complex on the track, in two parts. 8A deceives: a fast, wide entry that makes 8B -- extremely tight -- arrive much sooner than expected. It is a textbook slow-in, fast-out: place the car for 8A (enter about a car width off the right curbing, apex a few feet off it), but all focus belongs to 8B. Balance entry speed against braking through 8A, let the car straighten briefly, then brake HARD and scrub the speed; sit left of mid-track for a moment, keep some brake pressure on to keep the front weighted, turn quickly and rotate, and dive to the right curbing for the 8B apex. Back to throttle there, and let it carry out to the left. Some cars need second gear for the exit; others carry third.
8.name: Turn 8 (8A/8B)

tips.text: Two parts: fast entry, very tight exit. All focus belongs to the second part -- balance speed against braking through 8A, straighten briefly, then brake hard and scrub it.
Slow in, fast out: keep some brake pressure to weight the front, rotate the car, apex on the right curbing at 8B, and get back to throttle.

9.character: A left-hander whose real job is setting up Turn 10 -- Garagistic calls it 'the Setup'. Enter from far left for a late apex; it has positive camber and carries more speed than you think. Brake before turn-in, bring the car all the way to the right curbing, and get quickly back to throttle. But sacrifice a little if you must: what matters is arriving at Turn 10 set up far enough right. Track out only to mid-track, then hustle back right. Note the pit exit sits on the left at this corner's exit.
9.name: Turn 9

tips.text: This corner is a sacrifice for Turn 10 -- give up a little here if it buys arriving at 10 set up far enough right. (The pit exit is on your left at this corner's exit.)
Late apex with camber help: brake before turn-in, all the way to the right curbing, then quickly back to throttle -- out to mid-track only, then hustle back right for 10.
